findings.title: test
findings.text: This equality assertion can become vacuous. Both sides are produced by the code under test, and nothing pins that the two invocations actually select different contexts. If `corpus_set=parity_and_adversarial` stops adding a claim (REQ-0008 edited or removed, selector handling regressed to the default context), both runs report the same count and the test passes even with the swallowing bug restored — exactly the situation the file's own comment describes as "15 applying instead of 16". Anchor one side to an independent oracle: pin the literal count the comment already records (`assert_eq!(applying(&with), 16)`), or cross-check against `req select corpus_set=parity_and_adversarial` (counting its ` applies` lines) so the selection count comes from a different command path.

findings.title: test
findings.text: This test only proves `--pairs` did not consume `--gold`; it never proves `--gold` was honoured. The `# Tier-2 funnel:` header is printed (funnel.rs:445) *before* the gold file is opened (funnel.rs:484-491), so a run that accepts `--gold` and then fails to read it exits 3 and still passes both assertions — a `--gold` regression that loses the path or loads nothing stays green. Assert the section that only the honoured path can emit.

findings.title: documentation
findings.text: Adding a dedicated test file for `--pairs` makes AGENTS.md §Tier-2 funnel stale: it currently records "The flag is plumbing and carries no test of its own — recorded rather than implied." (AGENTS.md:322-323). Per this repo's rule that docs are claims, that sentence must be corrected in this same change — either reword it (the *parse* is now tested; the printed-list behaviour still is not) or add the missing positive assertion (with `--pairs` the proposal list is not truncated to 12, funnel.rs:471) and update the record accordingly. Note the test file also does not exercise `list_all` at all, so deleting `list_all = true` keeps every test here green.

findings.title: documentation
findings.text: The audit claim is inaccurate for `decision`. `decision::run` does not dispatch on `args.first()`; it iterates every argument (`for arg in args`, decision.rs:318-327) and accepts `--fill`/`--verify` with last-one-wins. Only `canon` uses `args.first()` (main.rs:425). Since this comment is the whole substance of the change and reads as a repo-wide audit result, keep it exact so the next maintainer trusting it does not skip re-checking `decision`.
